headline.text: On 28 February 2026, war involving Iran led to the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. Still showing in the data: about 3 ships a day in the latest reading to 22 November 2026, against a typical about 83 ships a day for this time of year.

In October 2026, the World Bank's fertilizer price index stood at 148 (2010 = 100), 6% higher than a year earlier. Prices: DAP US$803 a tonne; Urea US$420 a tonne. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year, in US dollars without adjusting for inflation. It is about 8% below the typical level. It is moving at about its usual pace for this time of year. Taking every line in this panel together, one is outside the range of past years.

Grain elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. It is the highest of the six comparable readings: this one and the past five years. It is about 2% above the typical level. It is moving at about its usual pace for this time of year. A new high or low on a figure that climbs year after year is the normal state, not a warning: it is the pace that would make it one. Canadian Grain Commission normally publishes weekly, but has published nothing since 4 October 2026, 52 days ago. This is the last figure it published, not a current one.

Ports shipped 3.21 million tonnes of grain abroad in the four weeks to 4 October 2026. It is inside the range of the past five years for this time of year. It is about 4% above the typical level. It is falling much faster than usual for this time of year. It has not yet passed the range of past years, so this is the earlier of the two signals. Canadian Grain Commission normally publishes weekly, but has published nothing since 4 October 2026, 52 days ago. This is the last figure it published, not a current one.

We follow 12 fresh fruits and vegetables at the Toronto wholesale market. In the latest week, two cost more and two cost less than at this time of year in any recent year, after allowing for inflation. Four are in their normal range, and for four we do not have enough past data. Four of the 12 are also rising or falling unusually fast, but no product sets off both checks at once. Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada normally publishes every business day, but has published nothing since 19 November 2026, 6 days ago. This is the last figure it published, not a current one.
In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row.

Of the 7 chains of knock-on effects we follow, 2 show readings that have moved along them. The furthest is “fertilizer imports are cut before seeding”, where the evidence has reached the link we call “stored supply is used up”.

The Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, run by the United Nations and the European Commission, lists eight serious disasters around the world. Three are in countries Canada buys food or farm supplies from. That tells us where to look; it does not mean Canada is affected.

questions.text: There is more grain in storage than in any recent year at this time. Is that a comfortable reserve, or grain waiting for trains and ships?

Wholesale prices for strawberries from the United States and peppers from Ontario are higher than in any recent year at this time. Is the cause weather where they are grown, the exchange rate, or something else?
Fewer ships than usual are passing through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Which Canadian imports and exports use these routes, and what are the alternatives?
Diesel costs more than at this time in any recent year, after inflation. How much of that reaches farm costs and grocery prices, and how soon?
